title: Stone wall built around Cedars of God grove
why: Earliest protective measure for the remaining cedars, aimed at keeping goats out; the grove had dwindled to about 16 old trees by 1697.

title: Order 144 makes shoreline inalienable public maritime domain
why: Legal basis still cited against coastal privatisation such as Dalieh and Eden Bay. Not confirmed on an opened page.

title: Litani River Authority established
why: Created to develop the Litani basin for power and irrigation; it later oversaw the Albert Naccache dam.

title: Electricite du Liban begins as state transport and power office
why: Origin of the utility, originally Office d'Electricite et des Transports en Commun; nationalised in 1964.

title: Qaraoun (Naccache) dam completed; Litani scheme built in stages 1962-66
why: Conflict: one source dates the dam 1959, the Litani page says the Naccache dam was completed 1962-1966 (corrected from 1959).

title: Electricity sector nationalised under EDL
why: State monopoly begins; decades later its deficits, over $30 billion cumulative, fed the fiscal collapse.

title: Reforestation drive plants 200,000 cedars
why: Of those planted, about 180,000 survived; a rare restoration success for the national emblem.

title: Dalieh of Raouche passes to private real-estate companies
why: Origin of the fight over Beirut's last public seafront; single-source, page could not be opened.

title: Al-Shouf Cedar Nature Reserve established, 550 km2
why: Largest reserve at about 5.3% of national territory; law number 532/1996 is search-reported only.

title: Naameh landfill opens south of Beirut
why: Meant as a stopgap, it ran until 17 July 2015, far beyond its capacity. (title corrected: source says Beirut and Mount Lebanon depended on the single Naameh landfill from 1997, not that it was an emergency site after Bourj Hammoud closed)

title: Qadisha Valley and Cedars of God inscribed on UNESCO list
why: Protected forest is only 10.2 ha with a 646 ha buffer zone.

title: Law 444 sets the environment protection framework
why: General environmental law; existence reported by search summary, text not opened.

title: Decree 8803 regulates quarries and crushers
why: Bars quarries from nature reserves and limits them to the eastern range; enforcement largely failed. Unopened source.

title: UNESCO names Shouf a Biosphere Reserve (~50,000 ha)
why: Extends protection to about 5% of Lebanon incl. Ammiq wetland; year confirmed 2005, 50,000 ha (corrected from 2005-07).

title: Bombing of Jiyeh plant spills about 30,000 t of fuel oil
why: Covered a third of the coastline and reached Syria; a benchmark for war-driven environmental damage.

title: Law 132 regulates offshore petroleum resources
why: Legal basis for licensing rounds; published in Official Gazette 41 on 2 Sep 2010.

title: Karadeniz powerships start supplying Zouk and Jiyeh
why: Supplied about a quarter of demand at high cost and emissions until the contract lapsed in 2021.

title: Bisri dam project begins with $474M World Bank financing
why: Total cost $617M; Islamic Development Bank and government covered the rest.

title: Naameh landfill closes; garbage crisis begins
why: Closed after taking far more than its design capacity, leaving Beirut and Mount Lebanon without a plan.

title: Over 100,000 join the garbage-crisis protests
why: Largest of the 'You Stink' demonstrations; first protest was 8 August 2015.

title: Law 51 approves World Bank loan for environmental pollution abatement
why: Financing for Litani-related pollution control; dated 24 Nov 2015, Official Gazette 48.

title: Cabinet picks Costa Brava and Bourj Hammoud coastal landfills
why: Temporary sea-edge dumps chosen after the crisis; reported by search summary only.

title: Parliament approves Minamata Convention accession
why: Mercury treaty accession passed at the 18 Jan 2017 session; law number not legible in the source.

title: Cabinet asks CDR to study expanding Costa Brava and Bourj Hammoud landfills
why: Costa Brava lasted five months against a planned 3.5 years, showing the stopgap failed. (title corrected: LBCI says cabinet asked the CDR to draft an expansion study within 15 days)

title: Law on petroleum sector transparency passed
why: Session of 24-25 Sep 2018; number and date garbled in the source text, so left blank. (corrected from 2018-10: Law 84/2018 ratified 10 October 2018)

title: Beirut air quality: carcinogenic particles reported doubled since 2017
why: Generators running 15-20 hours a day after 2021 became the main source; study-based, search-reported. (date corrected from 2019: the finding is from a study cited as Mehdy 2024)

title: Law 119 approves Kigali amendment to Montreal Protocol
why: Ozone and climate measure; Law 117 of the same date approved a FAO regional office.

title: Paris Agreement ratification law dated 29 March 2019 (Law 115/2019)
why: Number and date reported by search, inferred from neighbouring laws 117 and 119; not seen in text.

title: Law 127 joins Barcelona Convention protocol on protected areas
why: Covers specially protected areas and Mediterranean biodiversity; Official Gazette supplement 23.

title: 194 wildfires burn about 5,174 ha in Mount Lebanon
why: Days before the protest uprising; one civilian killed and international aircraft called in.

title: Law 146 approves French loan for Qadisha Valley sewage
why: Wastewater pilot in the UNESCO valley, dated 15 Oct 2019.

title: Lebanon formally becomes party to the Paris Agreement
why: Announced by the UN mission; signed in 2016, domestic law in 2019 per search.

title: World Bank freezes Bisri dam financing
why: Conditions on ecological compensation and operations unmet; the June 2020 date in some reports differs.

title: Laws 169 and 170 create Nmairiyeh and Abbasiyeh coastal reserves
why: New protected coastal sites, gazetted 14 May 2020. (corrected from 2020-05-08: Laws 169 and 170 dated 5 May 2020)

title: Port blast: 2,750 t ammonium nitrate, 218 dead
why: 124 m crater and about 300,000 displaced; seed of the silos collapse and later litigation.

title: World Bank cancels Bisri dam funding
why: Date corrected from 5 Sep (press); ecological plan, O&M plan and contractor mobilisation were missing.

title: More than 100 tonnes of carp die in Lake Qaraoun
why: Visible collapse of the Litani basin from untreated sewage, industry and runoff.

title: Solar adds about 100 MW, then about 500 MW in 2022
why: From 90 MW in 2020; installers grew from about 150 to 800 firms by 2023.

title: Updated NDC raises 2030 cut to 20% unconditional
why: Reported figures; UNDP page returned an access error, so not confirmed.

title: Karpowership halts supply over unpaid bills
why: Suspension in May, resumed in June as a goodwill gesture; prelude to the October cut-off.

title: Powership contract ends; EDL down to about 4 hours a day
why: Blackouts of up to 20 hours in Beirut; generators could not fill the gap.

title: First block of damaged Beirut port silos collapses
why: Two more collapses in August after grain fermented and burned for weeks.

title: QatarEnergy takes 30% of Block 4
why: Completes the consortium line-up with TotalEnergies and Eni ahead of drilling (corrected from 2023-01-30).

title: Drilling starts on Block 9 (Qana); well comes up dry
why: No commercial gas found; TotalEnergies said it remained committed to Lebanon (corrected from 2023-09).

title: Cross-border shelling starts; white phosphorus hits Dhayra on 16 Oct
why: First phosphorus attack documented; later soil tests found 1,858 ppm at some sites.

title: Nationwide blackout after fuel reserves run out
why: EDL fuel stocks fully depleted; illustrates the grid's fragility before the 2026 supply dip.

title: Ceasefire ends the main 2023-24 conflict phase
why: Period of primary documented environmental damage runs Oct 2023 to Nov 2024.

title: Over 65,000 olive trees destroyed; 22.5% of farmland affected
why: Assessment covers damage through end of 2024; about 38% of the national harvest.

title: War debris estimated at 16 million tonnes; disposal cost $145M
why: About 40 temporary storage sites identified; plan to recycle 70%.

title: Soil tests: chromium above limits in 45% of southern samples
why: Also zinc, copper and lead exceedances at some sites; contamination is uneven.

title: World Bank approves $250M LEAP project incl. rubble management
why: First phase of a $1B framework; needs estimated at $11B after the 2023-24 war.

title: Law 14 approves World Bank loan for renewable energy
why: Loan for the Lebanon Renewable Energy and Energy System Strengthening project; session of 30 Jun 2025.

title: Worst drought in 65 years; Qaraoun inflows 13% of normal
why: 44% of the population rely on trucked water; war damage to water systems put at $171M.

title: UNDP and Environment Ministry launch NDC 3.0 process
why: Update of 2035 targets; search-reported, UNDP page not opened. (corrected from 2026: search report dates the NDC 3.0 inception workshop 26 June 2025; UNDP page not opened)

title: Fourth offshore licensing round reportedly in preparation
why: Energy Minister said Lebanon is preparing a fourth offshore licensing round; fiscal and contractual amendments expected before cabinet within weeks (January 2026).

title: Block 8 permit signed by TotalEnergies, Eni and QatarEnergy
why: 35/35/30 split and 1,200 km2 of 3D seismic despite the Block 9 dry hole.

title: Reported aerial glyphosate spraying of about 8.5 km2 at the border
why: Single-source claim of concentrations 50 times agricultural use; not found on the Greenpeace page.

title: Hostilities resume, reopening environmental damage in the south
why: The date comes from the Greenpeace timeline; parliament extended its term a week later.

title: Cabinet reportedly lets cement firms run quarries on renewable permits
why: One-year permissions renewable up to ten years; search-reported, not opened.

title: Private generator tariff reaches 41,973 LBP per kWh
why: Generators remain the real grid for most households; EDL supply fell to about 4 hours in July.

title: EDL supply averages about 4 hours daily, down from 7-9 in February
why: A 1,000 MW capacity gap and $30B cumulative sector deficit.

title: Cabinet approves electricity reform policy to unbundle EDL
why: Policy paper dated 21 July; GENCOs, TRANSCO and regional distributors in phase two. Date corrected from 21 July.

title: Phosphorus munitions reported burning groves at Yaroun and Arnoun
why: Low-tier outlet; consistent with earlier patterns but needs corroboration (corrected from 2026-09-21).
